nodes.content: Design a mixed-criticality accelerator runtime guaranteeing control-task deadlines despite nonpreemptible inference kernels and shared-memory interference.
requirements: Under declared execution and interference bounds, all admitted control jobs meet 2 ms deadlines.
Guarantee starvation-free inference progress under adversarial arrivals without compromising admitted control deadlines.

nodes.content: Use admission-tested cyclic reservations with ≤200-µs inference slices, bounded memory interference, 2-ms control response checks, and guaranteed inference slots.
How should admission bounds account for kernel blocking and shared-memory contention while guaranteeing inference slots under adversarial control releases?
Per-2-ms-frame 200-µs inference reservations, 200-µs blocking, and bounded memory-stall charges keep admitted control responses ≤2 ms.
Derive admission inequalities from hypothesized reservation, blocking, and memory-stall bounds; implement the scheduler and stress-test deadlines and inference progress.
Run FrameStorm with adversarial control releases, 200-µs kernels, and bounded memory contention; measure 2-ms deadline misses and inference-slot occupancy.
FrameStorm: an admitted control job took 2.08 ms despite 180-µs blocking, two 200-µs frame reservations, and 100-µs in-bound stalls.
Charge two reservations per 2-ms response window, plus 200-µs blocking and bounded memory stalls; admit only if response ≤2 ms.
Sweep FrameStorm release offsets at 10-µs granularity under two-reservation admission; measure worst control latency and maximum inference-service gap.
FrameStorm offset sweep: zero of 100,000 admitted control jobs missed deadlines (worst 1.96 ms); inference received 200 µs per frame.
Adopt two-reservation admission checks with protected inference slots: FrameStorm exposed the prior undercount, and revised-admission sweeps met deadlines.
Implement FrameGuard with ≤200-µs certified inference kernels, protected per-frame slots, memory-bandwidth caps, and two-reservation admission checks.
FrameGuard v0.1 provides two-reservation admission checks, ≤200-µs kernel validation, protected inference slots, memory-bandwidth caps, and deadline telemetry.
How does FrameGuard prevent oversized kernels or excessive memory traffic from invalidating admitted control response bounds?
Use separate control/inference accelerator engines, partition DRAM bandwidth, and admit control by isolated worst-case bounds while reserving inference capacity.
First verify independent engine queues and enforceable DRAM quotas, then derive isolation-based admission tests and minimum inference-service guarantees.
Use FrameGuard v0.1 telemetry to probe engine-queue independence and DRAM quota enforcement under concurrent control releases and inference bursts.
EngineIsolation probe report contains concurrent-run queue-latency traces, per-engine DRAM counters, and quota-enforcement checks.
Audit EngineIsolation traces for queue independence and quota violations; compare FrameGuard reservations against dual-engine partitioning on latency and inference gaps.
EngineIsolation: independent queues and enforced 60/40 DRAM quotas yielded 1.72-ms worst control latency and ≤2-ms inference gaps.
Prefer dual-engine isolation where available: 1.72-ms worst control latency versus FrameGuard’s 1.96 ms; retain FrameGuard otherwise.
Fault-inject 250-µs launches into FrameGuard and DRAM quota overruns into both modes; verify rejection, throttling, deadlines, and inference service.
FaultInjection: oversized kernels were rejected and DRAM excess throttled, but certified 200-µs kernels completed 0/1,000: 12-µs dispatch exceeded reservation.
Can independent engine queues and enforced DRAM partitions guarantee inference progress despite dispatch overhead without violating control admission bounds?
With ≤12-µs dispatch, 60/40 DRAM-partitioned engines meet admitted 2-ms control deadlines and bound backlogged inference completion gaps to 2 ms.
Shared dispatch locking causes >2-ms inference gaps under adversarial control arrivals despite 60/40 DRAM quotas and intact control deadlines.
Use a debt-capped inference server guaranteeing minimum windowed service; admit control using dispatch-inclusive blocking and DRAM-interference bounds.
What debt cap and service window guarantee 200-µs inference kernels plus 12-µs dispatch without violating control admission?
Sweep debt caps and service windows across independent and shared-lock dispatch under adversarial arrivals; measure control deadlines and inference gaps.
With 212-µs debt caps and 2-ms windows, both dispatch modes had zero deadline misses and ≤1.99-ms inference gaps.
Randomize release phases over million-job shared-lock traces at 212-µs debt caps; measure inference completion gaps and dispatch-lock waits.
Million-job shared-lock traces exposed 2.14-ms inference gaps during 38-µs lock waits; admitted control jobs had zero deadline misses.
How should debt-capped inference service account for shared dispatch-lock waits without jeopardizing admitted control deadlines?
Capping dispatch-lock waits at 40 µs and reserving 252 µs per 2-ms window preserves control deadlines and inference progress.
Replay both debt-sweep and million-job traces with 40-µs lock caps and 252-µs reservations; measure deadline misses and inference gaps.
Replayed million-job traces with 40-µs lock caps and 252-µs reservations: zero control deadline misses; maximum inference gap 1.99 ms.
Adopt 252-µs inference reservations with 40-µs lock caps; the 212-µs setting missed the inference-gap target.
Use a persistent accelerator dispatcher with ≤100-µs nonpreemptible tiles, bank-partitioned memory, and admission-tested mandatory inference turns.
Certify ≤100-µs tiles and bank isolation, implement persistent dispatch, then compare deadline latency and inference gaps against 252-µs reservations.
Use EngineIsolation traces to configure bank partitions; certify ≤100-µs tiles and test persistent dispatch against adversarial control arrivals.
EngineIsolation v2 report replaces DRAM-quota checks with bank-partition certification and adds ≤100-µs tile certificates and persistent-dispatch latency traces.
Compare EngineIsolation v2 bank-isolation and tile traces against v1 quota traces; audit interference bounds and worst-case dispatch latency.
Audit confirmed EngineIsolation v2’s ≤100-µs tiles, ≤9-µs dispatch, and ≤25-µs bank interference; v1 lacked bank-isolation certificates.
Run TileStorm using audited EngineIsolation v2 bounds; compare persistent dispatch with 252-µs reservations on deadlines and inference gaps.
EngineIsolation v3 report replaces v2’s dispatch-only traces with TileStorm deadline and inference-gap comparisons against 252-µs reservations.
Audit EngineIsolation v3 TileStorm traces against v2 certificates; compute worst admitted control latency, inference gaps, and bound violations.
TileStorm: persistent dispatch had zero bound violations, 1.78-ms worst control latency, and 1.94-ms inference gaps versus 1.99-ms baseline.
Prefer certified persistent dispatch on bank-partitioned devices: TileStorm cut inference gaps to 1.94 ms with 1.78-ms control latency.
How can persistent dispatch enforce mandatory inference turns under continuous control arrivals without introducing unbounded control blocking?
Charging two mandatory 134-µs inference turns per control response window preserves admitted deadlines and guarantees backlogged inference progress.
Extend EngineIsolation v3 TileStorm traces with adversarial release phases; charge two 134-µs turns and measure deadline misses, inference gaps.
Adversarial TileStorm phases: two-turn admission yielded zero control deadline misses across 1 million jobs and maximum inference gap 1.97 ms.
Use release-aware guarded inference launches, admission-tested protected inference windows, and memory token buckets to bound control interference.
Derive guarded-launch and memory-token admission bounds atop certified persistent dispatch and two-turn accounting; stress-test deadlines and inference gaps.
Integrate EngineIsolation v3 tile certificates with FrameGuard v0.1 admission; implement release-aware launch guards and memory token buckets.
FrameGuard v0.2 adds certified ≤100-µs tiles, release-aware launch guards, memory token buckets, and two-turn control admission.
Run GuardStorm with adversarial releases and DRAM bursts, comparing FrameGuard v0.2 against two-turn TileStorm on deadline misses and inference gaps.
GuardStorm: FrameGuard v0.2 missed zero of 1 million control deadlines; worst latency 1.81 ms, inference gap 1.92 ms.
Choose FrameGuard v0.2 over persistent dispatch for shorter inference gaps; retain faster dual-engine isolation and 252-µs reservations as fallbacks.
